summary.text: A proton is a stable subatomic particle with a positive electric charge of +1 e.
One or more protons sit in the nucleus of every atom, and their number is the atomic number that defines the element.
A proton is not elementary: it holds three valence quarks, two up and one down, bound together by the strong force.

facts.label: Quark makeup
facts.value: Two up quarks and one down quark

facts.label: Named by
facts.value: Ernest Rutherford, for the hydrogen nucleus, in 1920

facts.label: Lone proton
facts.value: The nucleus of the most common hydrogen isotope

items.prompt: Two atoms have different numbers of protons in their nuclei. What must be true?

options.label: They have the same mass
They have different charges overall
They are atoms of different elements
They hold the same number of neutrons

items.explain: The number of protons is the defining property of an element.

items.prompt: What job do protons do for an atom's electrons?

options.label: They supply the attractive force that binds them
They push the electrons outward
They shield the electrons from each other
They carry the electrons around the nucleus

items.explain: Protons provide the attractive electrostatic force binding the electrons.

items.prompt: A proton's mass is mostly not the quarks' own weight. Where does the rest come from?

options.label: Extra neutrons packed inside the proton
Electrons trapped within the proton
Heavy quarks too small to detect
Binding energy: the quarks' motion and the gluon fields

items.explain: Quark rest masses add up to about 1% of a proton's mass, and the remainder is binding energy.

items.prompt: Rutherford knocked a particle out of the nucleus of one element by collisions, and it matched the lightest nucleus known. What did that suggest?

options.label: The particle was an electron in disguise
The particle might be a building block of heavier nuclei
The nucleus was made only of light atoms
The collision had created a brand new element

items.explain: The lightest nucleus extracted from heavier ones was a candidate to be a building block of them.

items.prompt: Early physicists treated the proton as indivisible. What does the Standard Model now say it is?

options.label: A composite particle containing three valence quarks
An elementary particle with no parts
A pair of electrons bound tightly together
A cloud of gluons with no quarks in it

items.explain: In the Standard Model protons are composite particles with three valence quarks.

items.prompt: At the center of the most common type of hydrogen atom, what sits in the nucleus?

options.label: One proton and one neutron
One proton and one electron
A single proton and nothing else
Two protons bound together

items.explain: The nucleus of the most common hydrogen isotope is a lone proton.
